subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 68-year-old man with Parkinson disease has been taking levodopa alone and develops nausea, lightheadedness, and worsening on-off fluctuations. His neurologist changes his regimen to a fixed combination of levodopa and carbidopa, and the nausea and blood pressure instability improve while his motor symptoms become more predictable.
question: Which of the following best explains the effect of carbidopa in this combination?

options.text: It inhibits catechol-O-methyltransferase in the central nervous system
It inhibits monoamine oxidase B and prolongs dopamine action
It is a direct agonist at dopamine D2 receptors
It inhibits DOPA decarboxylase in peripheral tissues, increasing delivery of levodopa to the brain
It blocks the blood-brain barrier to dopamine and reduces peripheral side effects

explanation_correct: Levodopa is a dopamine precursor that crosses the blood-brain barrier, whereas dopamine itself does not. Carbidopa inhibits aromatic L-amino acid decarboxylase (DOPA decarboxylase) in peripheral tissues but does not cross the blood-brain barrier, so a larger fraction of levodopa reaches the brain and is converted to dopamine there, while peripheral conversion to dopamine that causes nausea and hypotension is reduced.

explanation_incorrect.A: Catechol-O-methyltransferase inhibitors such as entacapone and tolcapone block methylation of catecholamines; carbidopa is not a COMT inhibitor.
explanation_incorrect.B: Monoamine oxidase B inhibitors such as selegiline reduce dopamine degradation in the brain; carbidopa does not inhibit monoamine oxidase.
explanation_incorrect.C: Carbidopa has no direct dopaminergic agonist activity; dopamine agonists such as pramipexole act at D2 receptors.
explanation_incorrect.E: Carbidopa does not block the blood-brain barrier; its effect reflects peripheral inhibition of DOPA decarboxylase, and it does not prevent dopamine formation in the brain.

educationalObjective: Carbidopa inhibits peripheral DOPA decarboxylase and thereby increases the fraction of levodopa that reaches the brain.
